name: Bridge Over Troubled Water
description: The middle two ranks are a river: primary movers cannot land in its water and line moves may cross between banks only through the d/e-file bridge.
ambiguities: The river is interpreted as ranks four and five, and the bridge as the four d/e-file squares in those ranks.
Bridge squares are landable; the other twelve river squares are water and cannot be primary destinations.
A rook, bishop, or queen crossing completely between banks must traverse the river only on files d/e. Other pieces use their primary destination.
Only the primary mover is constrained for castling, and promotion and en-passant use the pawn destination.

name: Reconnaissance
description: Captures are allowed only against piece types studied as ordinary legal capture targets on an earlier affected-player turn.
ambiguities: A target type becomes unlocked after completing a turn on which at least one standard-legal capture of that type was available, so it cannot be captured on the first study turn.
Study uses standard-legal rather than pseudo-legal captures and persists for the rest of the game.
Capturing promotions are classified by the captured target type; en-passant studies and captures pawns.
Exact initialization from an arbitrary midgame move list is impossible because unplayed historical capture opportunities are absent; chronological play from the game start is exact.
